### Feature Request

Can we add `info` to the `figures` object exported by `listr2`?

The existing object includes semantic symbols such as `tick`, `cross`, and `warning`, but it does not currently include an equivalent symbol for informational messages.

A possible implementation would be:

- Unicode: `ℹ`
- Fallback: `i`

This would allow consumers to use:

```js
import { figures } from 'listr2';
console.log(figures.info);
```

### Use Case

As a use case, `node-core-utils` already depends on `listr2` and is also depending on the standalone `figures` package for CLI status symbols.

I proposed a change to switch to figures utilities from `listr2` so that the redundant dependency could be removed. There's no `figures.info`, so we can't use the figures utility from listr2.

The other symbols mapped directly:
- success → `figures.tick`
- error → `figures.cross`
- warning → `figures.warning`

Adding `figures.info` would provide the appropriate semantic symbol and let us preserve the previous informational output without retaining another dependency.

Details: https://github.com/nodejs/node-core-utils/pull/1174#discussion_r3895616545

This creates many intermediate arrays per render (one per task in the tree) with zero throttling.

With ~30+ tasks and 93,000 output updates over 44 minutes, V8 accumulates garbage in the old generation faster than Mark-Compact can free it, eventually hitting the heap limit (2GB) with FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory.

The stack trace shows `Builtins_ArrayPrototypeFlatMap` and `Builtins_FlattenIntoArrayWithMapFn` repeated recursively, confirming the render path as the source.

No debounce/throttle exists between the event emission and the full tree re-render. A simple 33ms throttle or per-task (rather than global tree) rendering would prevent this.

body: Hi @cenk1cenk2, hope you're well! 👋 ### Replication of the Problem ```ts import { ListrTask /* ✅ error as expected with `verbatimModuleSyntax: true` */ } from 'listr2'; import { ListrTaskWrapper, /* 💥 no error as expected with `verbatimModuleSyntax: true` */ } from 'listr2'; ``` [TypeScript Playground](https://www.typescriptlang.org/play/?verbatimModuleSyntax=true#code/JYWwDg9gTgLgBAbzgGWAZxlAKgQzQazgHoAqOQUHI4BTKKaOPagDzCoGMYqATOAd2BgALOAAMAbjQBGOGKACyELgFcANlQDKATwB2MHEwBccTEqoi4JInAC+cAGZ0QcAOQr0mAEzOA3ACh-AYFBvqCQsIgo7th4+ADqUDhgrFAANMRkgLwbgKU7cNoQ1LT0jFQs7Jw8-EKiElDSsiAKympauvpGJmYWVrYOEE6uUV7eQA) ### Problem `TaskWrapper` is exposed as a runtime class in the typings, but isn’t exported as a value from [`dist/index.js`](https://unpkg.com/listr2@9.0.1/dist/index.js) or [`dist/index.cjs`](https://unpkg.com/listr2@9.0.1/dist/index.cjs), meaning that `verbatimModuleSyntax` misses reporting it as a problem if there is no `type` in the import. This leads to a situation where consumers can (incorrectly) import it as a value and receive a `SyntaxError` at runtime (eg. with [Node.js v22.18.0](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v22.18.0) type stripping): ```bash $ node index.ts import { Listr, ListrTaskWrapper } from 'listr2'; ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ SyntaxError: The requested module 'listr2' does not provide an export named 'ListrTaskWrapper' at ModuleJob._instantiate (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:228:21) at async ModuleJob.run (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:335:5) at async onImport.tracePromise.__proto__ (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:647:26) at async file:///Users/k/p/project/index.ts Node.js v22.18.0 ``` ### Suggested resolution Maybe make the public surface type-only (export a `ListrTaskWrapper` interface/type; keep the concrete class internal), eg. `export type { ListrTaskWrapper }` from the entry and stop re-exporting/mentioning the class in public types. ### Environment OS: macOS Sequoia 15.6 (24G84) Node.js version: v22.18.0 Terminal: Ghostty 1.1.3 listr2 version: 9.0.1 ### Log Output ```bash ``` ### Preflight - [x] Read/Search existing issues and the provided [documentation](https://listr2.kilic.dev). - [x] Be sure to not open an issue in the [looking for contributions section](/repository/contributions.html#looking-for-contributions). - [x] Checking the latest version of the software to confirm it has not been fixed already.

```ts
import { Writable } from 'stream'
import type { WriteStream } from 'tty'

/* istanbul ignore next */
export function createWritable (cb: (chunk: string) => void): NodeJS.WritableStream {
  const writable = new Writable()

  ;(writable as WriteStream).rows = Infinity
  ;(writable as WriteStream).columns = Infinity

  writable.write = (chunk: Buffer | string): boolean => {
    cb(chunk.toString())

    return true
  }

// #endregion

type _ = ReturnType<typeof createWritable>
```

I was porting some code from `listr` to `listr2` (thanks very much for this updated package!).

I was using a task like this with `ssh2-sftp-client`:

```ts
const tasks = new Listr([
  {
    title: `Connecting to ${passportUploadHost}`,
    task: () =>
      sftp.connect({
        host: passportUploadHost,
        username: passportUploadUser,
        password: passportUploadPassword,
        privateKey: sshKey,

])
```

### Replication of the Problem

### Problem

rxjs is used as a type-only import here: https://github.com/listr2/listr2/blob/365da3cbd79241051633e074bd6d075b9553673f/packages/listr2/src/interfaces/task.interface.ts#L1

But `Observable` makes it into the final typescript definition, forcing users of listr2 to have `skipLibCheck: true` in their `tsconfig.json`s or there will be this error when importing listr2:
```log
error TS2307: Cannot find module 'rxjs' or its corresponding type declarations
```

Using the `Observable` type from `rxjs` doesn't look correct as listr2 uses [its own `isObservable` function](https://github.com/listr2/listr2/blob/365da3cbd79241051633e074bd6d075b9553673f/packages/listr2/src/utils/environment/is-observable.ts#L5) instead of `rxjs`'s.

I suggest exporting an `ObervableLike` interface and re-use it in `isObservable` as TypeScript supports duck typing:

**NEW** `observablelike.interface.ts`
```ts
interface ObserverLike {
  next: (value: string) => void
  complete: () => void
  error: (err: unknown) => void
}

export interface ObservableLike {
  subscribe: (observer: ObserverLike) => unknown
}
```
**CHANGED** `is-observable.ts`
```ts
import type { ObservableLike } from '@interfaces'

export function isObservable<T> (obj: any): obj is ObservableLike
```
**CHANGED** `task.interface.ts`
```ts
export type ListrTaskResult<Ctx> = string | Promise<any> | Listr<Ctx, ListrRendererValue, ListrRendererValue> | Readable | NodeJS.ReadableStream | ObservableLike
```

### Feature Request

Currently, when `task.output` is called, `DefaultRenderer` is selected and `bottomBar` is set to false, only the latest `task.output` is rendered. For example, in:

```typescript
const tasks = new Listr(
  [
    {
      title: 'This task will execute.',
      task: async (ctx, task): Promise<void> => {
        task.output = 'I will push an output. [0]'
        await delay(500)

        task.output = 'I will push an output. [1]'
        await delay(500)

        task.output = 'I will push an output. [2]'
        await delay(500)
      }
    }
  ],
  { concurrent: false }
)

await tasks.run()
```

The output that would result would look something like:
```
  ✔ This task will execute
    › I will push an output. [2]
```

after execution
In some cases, it would be useful to verbosely log each output entry, resulting in:

```
  ✔ This task will execute
    › I will push an output. [0]
    › I will push an output. [1]
    › I will push an output. [2]
```

Potentially, this could be done by adding a multiline render option and having the DefaultRenderer store each output instead of discarding on each OUTPUT event from the task.

### Use Case

While the bottom bar is useful, it loses context as to what task it was performed under.

Being able to output multiple items under a single task would maintain the structure listr2 provides.
